behavior: Public leaderboard rank, exact absolute tie position, stale cursor recovery and slower percentages use bounded order-statistic indexes.
Rivalry skill preserves the twenty-board and two-query contracts, exact ties and separate public/artificial scopes.
Public predicates intentionally retain NOT disabled AND NOT is_test_driver. Existing reward counters additionally exclude deleted_at and therefore were not silently reused.
Artificial reads sum disjoint public and test-driver time trees. Ordinary PB writes maintain one time tree, avoiding duplicated public-plus-all writes.
PB insert/update/delete and player visibility changes maintain indexes transactionally in SQLite and PostgreSQL, with migration backfill before readers activate.
Top/neighbor windows limit keys from a partial visible-leaf index before authoritative PB/player joins; hidden rows never consume candidate slots. The key window and joins use one statement snapshot.
Explicit leaf identity supports variable-length identifiers including a leaf and internal branch with the same prefix, and exact stale cursors that stop at an internal prefix.

objective_review.rejected: An uncompressed thirty-two-prefix UUID index could add sixteen billion counters for five hundred million PBs. It was rejected before implementation.
objective_review.chosen: Compressed radix tie tree: one leaf per visible PB, branching nodes only at actual divergence. N through 2N-1 nodes per tied group; singleton times consume one leaf.
objective_review.read_cost: Time prefix lookup reads at most sixty-three fixed-domain nodes per disjoint population. Tie ordinal probes at most thirty-six UUID prefix levels with at most sixteen children per UUID level, plus one indexed root lookup. Physical B-tree probes remain logarithmic in index size.
objective_review.write_cost: One Fenwick path per affected disjoint population and only existing compressed tie ancestors (at most thirty-six), plus at most one branch and one leaf. PostgreSQL improvements skip common time ancestors, retaining the existing board-before-counter lock order.
objective_review.storage_limit: Exact tie ordering still requires an additional N through 2N-1 nodes across the visible PBs. If five hundred million PBs occupy one board this means five hundred million through approximately one billion tree rows. Storage and migration cost must be qualified on representative data; account count alone is not PB count.
objective_review.visible_window_cost: A partial visible-leaf index supplies at most limit+one or radius keys before authoritative joins. Existing legacy offset is capped at10000, so row work is bounded independently of hidden PB volume. This replaces the initially retained hidden-candidate scan after objective review.
objective_review.remaining_scope: Physical index probes remain logarithmic; representative database storage, write throughput and migration duration remain unmeasured at target population.
